newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Builders back Australia small business reform.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Builders back Australia small business reform.

text.p: The Australian government's new small business policies could lead to a A$1.0 billion efficiency gain in the building industry, an industry group said on Monday.

Master Builders Australia national executive director John Murray said the group was delighted that the government had recognised the importance of the building industry by giving a high priority to reforming building regulations and approvals.

"It is important that all states and territory governments embrace these reforms if Australia is to benefit from the (government's) commitment to cutting red tape and helping small business to grow," Murray said in a statement.
The Housing Industry Association Ltd also welcomed the reforms, saying they would significantly reduce the paperwork and compliance burden for small business.
Murray said under the reforms, more building applications and inspections would be carried out by accredited private sector building professionals and the approval process would be rationalised.
The creation of an Australian Building Products Systems Certification Scheme would also improve the lengthy processes involved in having new products accredited, he said.
In addition, the reforms should lead to the creation of a national framework of consumer protection to provide builders licensing and registration, and statutory and warranty indemnity insurance.
"This should result in the dismantling of the state governments' monopoly schemes for warranty protection," Murray said.
"Consumers will be the main beneficiaries from this reform."
Earlier on Monday, the Australian government announced a raft of small business reforms, including a one-year exemption from unfair dismissal rules for new employees.
It also exempted small business from keeping records to back their fringe benefits tax payments.
